<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916037_theRebbe_540" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916037_theRebbe_540__p007">
  <section v="18">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the settlements of Eisav are called such because they are in a contracted manner, in contrast to the settlements of Yaakov which are in an extended manner within the realm of Tikkun.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, that which they are called "the settlements of Eisav,"</t>
    <t s="1">even though the concept of settlement is specifically in Tikkun,</t>
    <t s="2">for even in Tohu there are aspects of the vessels,</t>
    <t s="3">and the aspect of the vessels is the concept of settlement,</t>
    <t s="4">except that the settlements of Eisav are in a contracted manner,</t>
    <t s="5">meaning,</t>
    <t s="6">that the concept of settlement that is in Tohu is in an aspect of contraction and diminution,</t>
    <t s="7">for in Tohu there were many lights and few vessels,</t>
    <t s="8">for the vessels were not at all proportionate to the lights,</t>
    <t s="9">because there was no proper mixture between the lights and the vessels.</t>
    <t s="10">(In addition to this, that even the vessels in and of themselves are few,</t>
    <t s="11">meaning,</t>
    <t s="12">that the concept of vessel within them is in a diminished state),</t>
    <t s="13">and this was the cause of the breaking of the vessels,</t>
    <t s="14">that the lights departed upward and the vessels broke and fell downward.</t>
    <t s="15">And this is what was innovated in the matter of Tikkun,</t>
    <t s="16">that a proper mixture was made between the lights and the vessels,</t>
    <t s="17">few lights and many vessels,</t>
    <t s="18">so that from this, in Tikkun, settlement is in abundance,</t>
    <t s="19">the settlements of Yaakov in an extended manner.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="19">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the settlements of Eisav are a preface to Yaakov's dwelling, as the soul's descent is to gather and refine the sparks of Tohu through the awe of G-d, transforming the land of Canaan into the land of Israel.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, even though the aspect of Tohu in and of itself is not according to the intent,</t>
    <t s="1">and as the statement,</t>
    <t s="2">"This judgment did not please Me,"</t>
    <t s="3">this is that the settlements of Eisav and his descendants were not treasured and important,</t>
    <t s="4">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="5">they are a preface to the matter of "And Yaakov dwelt... in the land of Canaan,"</t>
    <t s="6">for the entire matter of the commerce of the soul's descent below is from the aspect of the breaking of the vessels of Tohu,</t>
    <t s="7">as mentioned above.</t>
    <t s="8">And this is that after it writes "the settlements of Eisav in a contracted manner," it is written "And Yaakov dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings, in the land of Canaan,"</t>
    <t s="9">for the descent of the soul below is in order to refine the sparks of Tohu, as mentioned above,</t>
    <t s="10">and this is the concept of "And Yaakov dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings,"</t>
    <t s="11">that "sojournings" (megurei) is a term meaning a storehouse,</t>
    <t s="12">and like "one who gathers in summer,"</t>
    <t s="13">and it is the concept of gathering and refining the sparks of Tohu that were scattered through the breaking of the vessels.</t>
    <t s="14">For it is known</t>
    <t s="15">that the matter of the breaking of the vessels is that the vessels became separated from their connection,</t>
    <t s="16">and the parable for this is from the matter of letters,</t>
    <t s="17">that when they are connected in a single word,</t>
    <t s="18">then they bear within them the meaning of the word.</t>
    <t s="19">And like the letters bet, reish, vav, chaf,</t>
    <t s="20">that when they are connected together in the combination "baruch," they bear the intellect that is in the word "baruch,"</t>
    <t s="21">and when they are scattered from one another,</t>
    <t s="22">then only an impression of the intellect remains in each letter.</t>
    <t s="23">And so too is the matter of the breaking of the vessels of Tohu,</t>
    <t s="24">that the vessels became separated from their connection, etc.</t>
    <t s="25">And this is the concept of "his father's sojournings" (megurei aviv),</t>
    <t s="26">that the soul in its descent below gathers and refines the sparks of Tohu that were scattered, etc.</t>
    <t s="27">Now,</t>
    <t s="28">there is another explanation of "his father's sojournings" (megurei aviv),</t>
    <t s="29">that "sojournings" (megurei) is from the term meaning awe/fear,</t>
    <t s="30">and as the Maggid explained</t>
    <t s="31">(whose day of hilula is on the 19th of Kislev,</t>
    <t s="32">and also the matter of the redemption of our master, the Alter Rebbe, on the 19th of Kislev is connected to the matter of the hilula of the Maggid)</t>
    <t s="33">that "his father's sojournings" is the concept of awe of our Father in Heaven.</t>
    <t s="34">And it is necessary to explain the connection between the two explanations,</t>
    <t s="35">based on what was explained above</t>
    <t s="36">(section 8 and onward)</t>
    <t s="37">that the primary refinement within Tikkun is through the aspect of the Divine Daat,</t>
    <t s="38">which is the self-aware recognition that is above intellect,</t>
    <t s="39">which is the concept of "the ultimate knowledge is that we do not know."</t>
    <t s="40">And this is the concept of "his father's sojournings" from the term awe</t>
    <t s="41">(according to the second explanation),</t>
    <t s="42">the aspect of awe of shame,</t>
    <t s="43">which comes from the recognition of the sublimity of Ein Sof that is beyond comprehension,</t>
    <t s="44">the aspect of "the ultimate knowledge is that we do not know."</t>
    <t s="45">And from this recognition comes the choice of good</t>
    <t s="46">(as mentioned above),</t>
    <t s="47">through which is the primary gathering and refinement of the sparks</t>
    <t s="48">(the first explanation of "megurei").</t>
    <t s="49">And this is also that the land of Israel is called here by the name "land of Canaan,"</t>
    <t s="50">for the matter of Canaan is as it is written, "Canaan, in his hand are deceitful scales,"</t>
    <t s="51">that through deceit a mixture of good and evil is made,</t>
    <t s="52">and as mentioned above</t>
    <t s="53">(section 6)</t>
    <t s="54">that from the matter of cunning a mixture of good and evil is made,</t>
    <t s="55">and it is the aspect of the externality of Daat,</t>
    <t s="56">which is the cause of the breaking of the vessels of Tohu.</t>
    <t s="57">But the purpose of this descent is to make from the land of Canaan the land of Israel,</t>
    <t s="58">which is the ascent that is brought about through the descent,</t>
    <t s="59">and according to the second explanation that "Canaan" is a term for a merchant,</t>
    <t s="60">which is the concept of the profit that comes through dispersion.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="20">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section connects the concepts to the imprisonment and redemption of the 19th of Kislev, where the ultimate descent was for the sake of ascent, leading to the revelation of Divinity and the spreading of the wellsprings of Chassidus outward.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is also the matter of the imprisonment and redemption of the 19th of Kislev,</t>
    <t s="1">that during the imprisonment there was the ultimate descent,</t>
    <t s="2">and as is known</t>
    <t s="3">that our master, the Alter Rebbe, then suffered bodily afflictions and afflictions of the soul, etc.</t>
    <t s="4">But the purpose of this descent is for the sake of ascent,</t>
    <t s="5">which is that at the time of the redemption, "all the ends of the earth saw," etc.,</t>
    <t s="6">and it is the concept of the revelation of Divinity through the signs and wonders performed by the tzaddikim,</t>
    <t s="7">and then the primary matter of "spread forth"</t>
    <t s="8">"your wellsprings outward" began,</t>
    <t s="9">and behold, through the spreading of the wellsprings of the inner dimension of the Torah, "he will come speedily,"</t>
    <t s="10">for then there will be the revelation of the inner dimension of Daat,</t>
    <t s="11">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="12">"For the earth will be filled with knowledge of Havayah," etc.,</t>
    <t s="13">speedily, literally.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
